messages:
lia-cs: Hey team — Maria from Skylane is hitting intermittent 401s during SDK onboarding and then a burst of 429s a few seconds later. She says it started after they added a short-lived token refresh flow. Sample log she pasted: `auth: failure, code=401, reason=token_expired` then `request_id=xyz, status=429, reason=rate_limit`
maria-customer: Confirming. We refresh tokens every 5s to keep session alive for edge clients (mobile), but about 1/20 requests fail with 401 then several 429s for 10s. Our dashboard shows many preflight calls from many devices.
sam-engineer: Thanks — two quick things to confirm: 1) are you reusing client instances or creating a new SDK client for each request? 2) what region are you pointing to (us-west/us-east)? If the client spins up new connections, we might be hitting short windows of token churn + regional routing mismatch.
maria-customer: We create a new client per user session (mobile background tasks). Region is hard-coded to eu-central. We have users in EU and NA.
sam-engineer: Hmm. Creating new clients per request + per-device token refresh can cause a preflight fanout to auth + edge which can show up as a 429 from our gateway while auth returns 401 for mismatched token TTL. Can you paste the snippet where you set up the SDK?
maria-customer: Sure: ```js const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: ephemeralToken, region: 'eu-central', retry: { maxRetries: 2 } }); await client.generate(prompt); ```
lia-cs: Also noted they're using ephemeral tokens minted by their own auth proxy with a 7s TTL. They said 5s refresh.
sam-engineer: Root cause hypothesis: token TTL is too short and your refresh jitter aligns badly across devices, producing many nearly-simultaneous preflight handshakes and some stale tokens hitting the runtime (401). The gateway then applies a burst protection policy which returns 429s to backpressure the downstream. Fixes: 1) increase TTL on ephemeral tokens to 30s or 60s; 2) reuse SDK client per app process; 3) add jitter to refresh (random 0-3s) and exponential backoff on 429s.
ben-ops: Can we confirm our gateway logs for request_id=xyz around 1767890005? deploy-bot: log-extract job queued: /logs/1767890000/request_id=xyz (attached)
sam-engineer: Thanks deploy-bot — log extract shows auth service returning 401 for token signature mismatch for ~6 requests then gateway returning 429 for ~120 requests in a 15s window.
maria-customer: If we increase TTL to 30s and reuse the client, how quickly should we expect it to resolve? Any config we need to change on our end for region routing?
sam-engineer: Should see normalisation within a minute after rollout. For region routing: remove hard-coded region or let SDK pick nearest region (set region: 'auto') — that avoids cross-region handshake storms. Also set `clientOptions.pool = true` (or reuse a singleton client).
lia-cs: I'll propose these changes to Maria and schedule a 30-min enablement call tomorrow 10:00 AM PT to watch metrics live. Action items: lia-cs -> coordinate the call; maria -> toggle TTL & client reuse in canary; sam -> stand by to watch logs and advise.
maria-customer: Thanks — I'll try increasing TTL to 30s and update to a single client instance per app process, add jitter. Will report back in this thread before the call. :pray:
sam-engineer: Also adding a small snippet for recommended refresh with jitter: ```js // pseudocode draw jitter const jitterMs = Math.floor(Math.random()*3000); setTimeout(refreshToken, 5000 + jitterMs); ```
lia-cs: Great. Noted renewal risk lowered if this gets fixed quickly — I'll mark the account health as "at-risk -> watching" and loop in renewals if still flapping after the enablement session.
ben-ops: I'll add a temporary soft-throttle exemption in the gateway for their IP range for the duration of the call so we don't double-throttle while they test. (expires automatically).
maria-customer: Appreciate it everyone — will update by EOD.
sam-engineer: Nice, and if any 401s persist after TTL bump, paste the full auth header (redact creds) and we'll inspect signature timestamps for clock skew.
